editorial:
If you grew up watching the original TV show, you already know the vibe: slow-motion beach runs, red swimsuits, and lifeguards who act like cops. The 2017 movie version leans hard into that silly energy. Dwayne Johnson plays Mitch Buchannon, the head lifeguard who takes his job way too seriously. Zac Efron plays Matt Brody, a disgraced Olympic swimmer forced to join the team as part of his community service. The two clash right away, and their back-and-forth banter drives most of the comedy. The story kicks off when Mitch notices strange drug activity near the beach and starts digging, even though the police tell him to stay out of it.

The action scenes are big and loud, with boat chases, explosions, and plenty of slow-motion running. Johnson and Efron have solid chemistry, and the supporting cast keeps things moving. The humor is crude and raunchy, so it is not for everyone, and the plot is pretty thin. But if you want a dumb, fun beach movie with big laughs and bigger muscles, this delivers. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final act, Mitch and Brody discover that Victoria Leeds, the wealthy club owner, is running a drug smuggling operation through the bay. They crash her private party, fight her henchmen, and chase her onto a boat. After a wild shootout, Victoria is arrested and the beach is saved. Mitch gets his job back, Brody earns his spot on the team, and the crew celebrates with a classic slow-motion beach run. The movie ends on a goofy, feel-good note that sets up more adventures.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dumb, fun action comedies with big laughs and beach vibes.
